title: A map quiz on iron ore
body: Meena's class is playing a map quiz on the iron ore belts of India. Each team must identify a belt from three clues. Meena's clue card reads: 'Clue 1: The hills here got their name because they look like the hump of an ox. Clue 2: The range has 14 deposits of super high grade hematite, which has the best physical properties needed for steel making. Clue 3: Ore from these mines is sent to Japan and South Korea through a port on the east coast.' Her teammate Arjun first guesses a belt in Karnataka, remembering that one famous mine there is named after a horse's face and is a 100 per cent export unit. Meena reminds him that the clue mentions an ox, not a horse, and points to a district in Chhattisgarh on the map.

title: Choosing a site for a power station
body: A state government wants to build a large thermal power station and a steel plant. Planners compare two sites. Site 1 lies close to a major coalfield in the Damodar valley, about 20 km from the mines. Site 2 lies near a big city about 900 km away, where most of the electricity and steel will finally be used. One planner argues that Site 2 is better because it is close to the market. Another points out that the plant will burn thousands of tonnes of coal every day, and that after burning, a large part of what arrives is left behind as ash. After studying the costs of moving raw material and the finished product, the planners choose Site 1 and decide to send electricity to the city through transmission lines.
